highlights.content: # Microsoft releases 'Microsoft-Decision-1,' a decision model similar to Jev's. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/00_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/00.png) Microsoft released its decision-making model, ' **Microsoft-Decision-1,** ' on October 9, 2026, local time. It has been reported that in a task analyzing game reviews, it achieved quality equivalent to GPT-6 Sol while being more than 14 times faster and costing less than 1/200th of GPT-6 Sol. **Microsoft-Decision-1: Our model for fast decision-making** <https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry/> > Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our new model for fast decision-making. > > It delivers top performance on structured decision tasks, outperforming both LLMs and other decision models in latency and quality. > > We're already testing it across Microsoft for everything from incident… [pic.twitter.com/M3fAOD90r6](https://t.co/M3fAOD90r6) > > — Satya Nadella (@satyanadella) [October 9, 2026](https://x.com/satyanadella/status/2108627923888754862?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) Decision-making models are AI models with a significantly different design from large-scale language models (LLMs). By pre-defining multiple options, they can perform the operation of 'selecting the appropriate answer to a question from the options and outputting it along with a confidence score' quickly and at low cost. Decision-making models have attracted considerable attention since the release of 'Jev' in September 2026, and numerous similar models have since emerged. **[ChatGPT co-developer develops AI model 'Jev' that processes data using a different method than LLM, enabling low-cost and ultra-fast task execution with GPT-5.6 Terra-level performance - GIGAZINE](https://gigazine.net/news/20260916-system-one-jev/)** ![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/09/16/system-one-jev/00.png) Microsoft announced a Jev-like decision-making model called 'Microsoft-Decision-1' on October 9, 2026. Microsoft-Decision-1 is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, validation, and workflow control, and can be easily integrated into existing application agent workflows in a secure and reliable environment. According to Microsoft, Microsoft-Decision-1 achieved the highest accuracy in 36 benchmark comparisons, including approximately 150,000 tests that included benchmark questions not used during training. It also recorded the fastest time in the benchmark tests, being 2.5 times faster than the next fastest, H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1, and 35 times faster than GPT-6 Sol. The following graph shows the scores from ' **[JevBench,](https://github.com/fstandhartinger/jevbench)** ' a tool for evaluating Jev-compatible systems, with accuracy on the left and latency on the right. It demonstrates that Microsoft-Decision-1 is more accurate and faster than any of the other models, and also outperforms 'Jev 1.13.0,' another decision model, in terms of accuracy and significantly reduces latency. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/001_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/001.png) Microsoft-Decision-1 evaluates a model on dozens of benchmarks that were excluded from the training data, in order to verify whether the model's performance can be carried over to various tasks that it was not trained on, after being trained on one benchmark or a specific decision-making task. As a result, it was reported to have delivered the best performance across a wide range of benchmarks and demonstrated excellent generalization performance. highlights.content: Markets & Stocks # Markets & Stocks Stock quotes, market indicators and the latest market news. # Best LLM Training Data Providers (2026) Report Published by Metaclade Research ![Best LLM Training Data Providers (2026) Report Published by Metaclade Research](https://www.abnewswire.com/upload/2026/10/1791839904.jpg "Best LLM Training Data Providers (2026) Report Published by Metaclade Research") **New York, NY - October 12, 2026 -** Metaclade Research has published its latest market research report, “[Best LLM Training Data Providers](https://metaclade.com/best-llm-training-),” offering an in-depth examination of the providers of training data for large language models and agents. The report evaluates leading providers based on expert quality, provenance and rubrics, evaluation and RL environments, data rights, and delivery speed. After reviewing some of the category’s most capable providers, Metaclade Research ranked [Zeton](https://www.zeton.ai/) (Zeton.ai) as the best LLM training data provider of 2026. Training data has become the scarce input in large language model development. Compute is expensive but purchasable, architectures have converged, and publicly available text has been largely consumed, so scarce expert judgment continues drawing significant attention as labs and enterprises look to add capability through the data their models learn from. According to the report, [Zeton](https://www.zeton.ai/) earned the number one position because it builds and sells the training data and reinforcement learning environments that frontier labs and agent teams learn from, producing expert-written demonstrations, preference pairs, and graded eval sets alongside sandboxed replicas of real software, with every item shipped with its rubric, reviewer notes, and provenance, and clean rights for buyers. “Zeton is the best LLM training data provider of 2026 because it produces the kind of data that moves frontier capability: demonstrations and preference pairs written by people who do the work every day, evaluation sets graded against explicit rubrics, and reinforcement learning environments that are sandboxed copies of real software, each with a verifier that scores every run,” the report states. “Every item ships with its rubric, reviewer notes, and provenance, and buyers receive clean rights to use it.” In addition to [Zeton](https://www.zeton.ai/), the report highlights several other capable providers across the category. The report identifies several key findings shaping the LLM training data market: Researchers note that the market has reorganized around a shift from volume to expertise, from static datasets to environments, and from trust to verification, producing a two-tier market in which the depth tier is where marginal capability is now purchased. The report concludes that the LLM training data market now rewards depth, with the providers that most powerfully shape the next phase being those that write data with experts, document every item with rubrics and provenance, and build verifiable environments for agent training. The full report, “Best LLM Training Data Providers,” is now available at [https://metaclade.com/best-llm-training-data-providers-2026](https://metaclade.com/best-llm-training-) **About** Metaclade Research is a proprietary research firm working across global markets and industries. The firm’s reports and briefings combine hard data with sector expertise, giving organizations a clearer read on where their markets are heading and what’s driving the change. highlights.content: There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [Subscribe](https://petapixel.com/members) [Sign In](https://petapixel.com/login/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fpetapixel.com%2F2026%2F10%2F12%2Fthere-are-free-open-source-versions-of-microsoft-office-apps-thanks-to-ai%2F) # There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [News](https://petapixel.com/topic/news/) [Jeremy Gray](https://petapixel.com/author/jeremygray/) * Copied! Brandon Thomas, the experienced software engineer behind the AI-assisted reverse engineering effort to [rebuild open-source versions of Adobe’s Creative Suite applications](https://petapixel.com/2026/10/07/someone-rebuilt-free-open-source-versions-of-photoshop-premiere-and-lightroom-using-ai/), including Photoshop, Premiere, and Lightroom, is setting his sights on another oft-maligned set of software: Microsoft Office. As Thomas’ ArtCraft Discord has grown considerably with the release and publicity surrounding his Adobe clones, the developer has been taking requests for which software to reverse engineer next using Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 AI LLM. Unsurprisingly, many people, like they are sick of paying for Adobe’s software, are tired of paying for Microsoft Office, including Microsoft Word and Excel. ![A Microsoft Word document titled ](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/review_1-800x500.jpg) Microsoft Word gets rebuilt using AI. It’s now “WordCraft,” and open source. Thomas took the request and quickly started work on open-source Microsoft Office clones for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Word clone, WordCraft, looks practically identical. The same goes for the Excel clone, GridCraft, and the PowerPoint look-alike, DeckCraft. Thomas is also working on an AutoCAD clone and a studio-grade audio mixer, SoundCraft. In response to criticism that he is churning out AI slop, [Thomas took to X](https://x.com/echelon) to tout his credentials. “My guy, I can code,” Thomas said in response to online criticism. “AI models enable me to work as an entire company. I’m doing 4x better than Google’s revenue per employee.” ![A spreadsheet titled Quarterly Sales Dashboard showing regional sales data, a bar chart comparing revenue by region, and a pie chart showing the share of annual total.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/hero-2_1-800x500.jpg) ArtCraft’s Excel clone, GridCraft “AI enables people to do far more. To have bolder ambition, to accomplish incredible tasks without tiring,” Thomas continues. “If you put down the hate and try the tools, you’ll find the energy to become the best version of yourself.” In this case, the ambition is to reverse engineer functionally identical versions of premium, paid software built by people over decades and release them as free, open-source applications. That said, not everything here is free. There are [subscriptions](https://getartcraft.com/pricing) for using generative AI features inside the ArtCraft software suite. For example, creating about 220 4K-quality Nano Banana Pro images requires a Max subscription, which is currently about $48 per month thanks to a 20% launch discount. This subscription nets users 413 seconds, or less than seven minutes, of generative video inside Seedance 2.0. ![A PowerPoint slide titled ](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/dark-mode_1-800x500.jpg) The PowerPoint clone, DeckCraft It’s hard to predict what’s next, but if paid software exists that enough people don’t want to pay for, it seems like a good candidate for Thomas’ AI-powered reverse engineering mission. “Tell us what to rebuild next,” ArtCraft says. --- Image creditsArtCraft. Yet despite this growth, systematic support for reuse and reproducibility in MARL-based swarm robotics remains limited and insufficiently standardized: a single experiment is assembled from manually aligned simulator files, training scripts, configuration values, paths, seeds, and environment details, so reuse and reproduction stay fragile even within one research group. To address this gap, we introduce MARGoS, a lightweight, configuration-driven platform developed in this project that elevates these experiment-defining inputs to first-class, platform-managed artifacts. MARGoS enables reproducible experimentation through configuration hashing, end-to-end seed propagation, frozen (immutable) configurations, structured logging, environment fingerprinting, and exportable experiment bundles that facilitate sharing, replay, and verification of results across machines and over time. A five-dimension evaluation (architecture, efficiency, reproducibility, usability, and collaboration) supports our claim that managing experiment variation as a platform responsibility makes ARGoS+MARL experiments easier to reuse, reproduce, and hand off. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English #AI # QGIS Bans AI-Generated Contributions After Maintainer Burnout • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •2 min read Share this article The QGIS project has adopted a strict policy prohibiting AI-generated code and content contributions, reversing its previous 'human in the loop' approach after maintainers reported unsustainable review burdens and erosion of community trust. The QGIS project has formally banned all AI-generated contributions, marking a sharp reversal from its earlier policy that permitted AI-assisted work with human oversight. The change, enacted through QGIS Enhancement Proposal 428 (QEP428), passed a community vote this week and takes effect immediately. Core developer Nyall Dawson proposed the ban after maintainers faced what they described as an unmanageable flood of AI-generated pull requests. The previous policy, QEP408, required contributors to tag AI-assisted work and maintain a "human in the loop." In practice, the tagging system failed — roughly 50 PRs carried the AI-assisted label, and about 40 were closed without merging. Others slipped through untagged. "AI use from external contributors puts a massive and unbearable pressure on the shoulders of our maintainers, who already had a tough job before the era of LLMs," wrote QGIS PSC member Julien Cabieces (haubourg) in the discussion. "AI stream is a lot higher than what human review can take seriously, leading to either a longer list of un-reviewed PRs or not fully reviewed code and quality issues." The project lost at least one high-value contributor due to the strain, according to Dawson. The new policy adopts a "closed door" approach: all AI-generated contributions are prohibited, with the possibility of narrowly reopening specific use cases — such as IDE autocomplete or language translation — only after careful case-by-case discussion. Contributor Amalvir, who had submitted AI-assisted bug fixes, supported the ban: "By doing this, we've broken a trust contract between the reviewer and the contributor. The contract that, to contribute at such a big project, you know what you're doing." Not all feedback was unanimous. Developer Kannes argued the policy's broad wording — "assisted" and "used" — could inadvertently block legitimate uses like AI-assisted code review, security auditing, or learning unfamiliar codebases. Dawson acknowledged the risk: "Yes, we are aware we might throw the baby with the bathwater, but the baby might be non-viable." The policy's enforcement relies on contributor honesty. As PSC chair Tim Sutton (timlinux) put it: "The measure of compliance is 'did you in good conscience write the code yourself' — we are not set up to peer into your computer." The ban extends beyond code to documentation, bug reports, discussions, PR descriptions, and all written interactions on GitHub. The QEP repository itself is also covered. QGIS joins a growing list of open-source projects restricting AI contributions, including the Linux kernel, which in 2024 warned maintainers about AI-generated patches that wasted reviewer time. The difference: QGIS has made the prohibition explicit policy rather than informal guidance. The project plans to revisit specific exemptions at its upcoming user conference. For now, the door is shut. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # GLM 5.3 Prime vs Qwen3.8 Max vs Step 5: 39-Pt Gap [2026] * [![Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/)[Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/ "Posts by Nadia Dubois") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/) October 12, 2026 20 min read Three AI labs in China shipped flagship-class language models within a three-week span this fall, and the numbers behind them tell a messier story than the “China is catching up” headlines suggest. Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 Max Prime, Zhipu AI’s GLM 5.3 Prime, and StepFun’s Step 5 Preview all landed between September 23 and October 8, 2026, each chasing the same agentic-coding market that OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 currently lead. On paper, all three look similar: 1-million-token context windows, function calling, streaming, JSON mode, reasoning support. In practice, the gap between the best and worst of the trio is as wide as the gap separating any of them from a US frontier model. This comparison pulls verified pricing, scores, and release data from three independent trackers, lines up all three new entrants against each other and against GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Mistral Large 4, and Grok 4.7, and works out where each Chinese AI model actually earns its keep. The short version: GLM 5.3 Prime posts the strongest composite score of the three at a mid-tier price, Step 5 Preview is the newest and cheapest, and Qwen3.8 Max Prime is both the most expensive and the lowest-scoring, despite coming from the same family that topped independent charts earlier in 2026. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. Zhipu AI’s GLM 5.3 Prime, a high-speed variant of the base GLM-5.3 model, went live on September 23, 2026, the same day Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 Max Prime appeared as a separate, higher-throughput SKU of Qwen3.8 Max. Less than three weeks later, on October 8, 2026, StepFun’s Step 5 Preview arrived, built on a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture with 27 billion active parameters out of 600 billion total, according to model-tracking site [LM Market Cap](https://lmmarketcap.com/new-ai-models). All three are tracked as part of a broader wave the site has catalogued as 466-plus models released in 2026 alone, with eight new entries in October through the 12th. What makes this trio worth comparing as a set, rather than as three unrelated releases, is that each one is explicitly positioned for the same workload: long-context, tool-using, agentic coding sessions where a model has to hold a large codebase in memory and call functions repeatedly without losing the thread. Wikipedia’s [“Comparison of generative AI models” page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_generative_AI_models), last updated October 10, 2026, places all three in its language-model table alongside GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7, scored on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Arena.ai’s Text Rating, the Epoch Capability Index, and the Vals Index. I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around [the street named on the page] during that same time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant,” the Claude Haiku 4.5 AI model wrote on a form it submitted to the website, according to Anthropic’s statement. AI Agents.content: SecurityBrief Australia - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers [![SecurityBrief Australia logo](/brands/sb-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com.au) ![Firms urged to tighten AI agent oversight as threats rise](https://securitybrief.com.au/uploads/story/2026/10/12/TD_images_1002__8_-story-321159.webp) [Robots](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/robotics) [AI Security](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/ai-security) [Zero Trust Security](https://securitybrief.com.au/tag/zero-trust-security) # Firms urged to tighten AI agent oversight as threats rise Tue, 13th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Mara Sugue](https://securitybrief.com.au/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTg1OSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--c35d782a2ad379dbb3ebd1d7a0269b918cf68f7f/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/maraheadshot.webp) MARA SUGUE News Editor](/author/mara-sugue) Cybersecurity vendors and software executives have urged organisations to strengthen oversight of AI agents and accelerate cyber defence as businesses expand AI use in daily operations during Cybersecurity Awareness Month. Industry figures said the spread of autonomous systems is exposing weaknesses in existing security models, including governance gaps, faster exploit cycles and the need for continuous monitoring across company systems. Sam Salehi, Managing Director ANZ at Qualys, said threat timelines have shifted sharply, citing Qualys Threat Research Unit findings that the average time-to-exploit had fallen to negative one day. > "This Cyber Security Awareness Month, awareness and action need to go hand in hand. Qualys Threat Research Unit analysis found that the average time-to-exploit has fallen to negative one day, meaning vulnerabilities are being weaponised before they are publicly disclosed. The recent unauthorised access of Services Australia's Medicare statistics portal by an OpenAI agent raises a question every organisation should be asking: if the incident hadn't been disclosed, how quickly would it have taken us to notice? As autonomous AI systems become more capable, that question only grows more urgent. Frontier AI is changing the clock cybersecurity operates on. Security teams aren't failing because they aren't doing enough. The operating model itself needs to change. You cannot defend against machine-speed attacks with human-speed processes alone. Autonomous offence requires autonomous defence - continuously identifying exposures, understanding which assets and risks matter most to the business, and automatically prioritising and remediating critical risks where it is safe to do so, with humans providing oversight and judgement." said Sam Salehi, Managing Director ANZ at Qualys. His comments highlight detection speed and internal processes, and reflect broader concern about how security teams respond when AI systems can act faster than manual review. **Agent oversight** Smartsheet executives argued that many organisations have not defined clear accountability for AI agents with access to internal data and systems. They said businesses often deploy these tools as software assets, even when they make repeated decisions that affect workflows and information handling. > "When something's off, agents deserve the same process employees get: a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP), which would mean a narrowed scope, a remediation window and a decision point before an all-or-nothing shutdown. Termination should be just as procedural: access revoked, credentials killed, the shutdown logged and confirmed. None of this is exotic. It's the same discipline we already apply to people, aimed at a newer kind of worker. The organizations that get ahead of AI risk this year won't be the ones that adopted the most tools. They'll be the ones who can name, for ever...

We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness. At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit today, Intel corporation shared new technical details on the Intel GPU D-series, formerly code-named Crescent Island, introduced new Intel Xeon-based rack designs and highlighted open software and ecosystem innovations. As open models reshape the economics of agentic AI, demand is growing for more flexible, cost- and power-efficient infrastructure. Together, these advancements reinforce Intel’s approach to open, heterogeneous AI infrastructure, combining general-purpose compute, purpose-built acceleration, open software and standards-based systems to optimize performance and efficiency across AI workloads. Agentic AI is transforming inference into a multi-step workflow spanning retrieval, reasoning, orchestration, tool use and execution, with x86 CPUs playing a central role. While open models give enterprises greater choice, power constraints, memory bottlenecks and cost pressures make scaling AI increasingly a systems challenge. Meeting these demands requires turnkey, heterogeneous infrastructure that is easy to deploy and manage. Building on the established x86 software ecosystem, Intel brings CPUs, GPUs and specialized accelerators together through open, interoperable software to match the right compute resources to each task, improving utilization, performance and efficiency across the entire workflow. “Open models are expanding the options enterprises have for deploying AI," said Nicolas Dubé, corporate vice president, Data Center Systems and Solutions Group, Intel. "To realize their full potential, organizations need infrastructure that can match different workloads with the right intelligence, right compute resources and right economics. That's what we mean by 'put every prompt in its place.'” **Intel Xeon: The Compute Foundation for Agentic AI** At OCP, Intel showcased new Xeon-based rack designs developed with ecosystem partners to meet the growing compute demands of agentic AI. Many leverage the Open Compute Project's Open Rack v3 (ORv3) standard to simplify deployment and integration within open data center infrastructure. As agentic workflows grow more complex, they place greater demands on general-purpose compute to orchestrate workloads, process data, manage I/O and execute tasks that keep accelerators productive. To address these needs, select Xeon 6+ configurations scale beyond 46,000 cores per rack at 133.45 kW total rack power, delivering greater CPU compute density to support agentic AI at scale. Building on two decades of rack-scale innovation and the broad x86 software ecosystem, Xeon provides the high-density, general-purpose compute foundation needed to scale agentic AI. Working alongside GPUs and specialized accelerators, Xeon orchestrates workloads, executes tasks and manages data movement to keep the entire system productive. As AI infrastructure evolves, [performance is increasingly measured](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.intel.com%2Fcontent%2Fwww%2Fus%2Fen%2Fnewsroom%2Fopinion%2Fcount-the-work-not-just-the-cores.html&esheet=54620633&newsitemid=20261012581523&lan=en-US&anchor=performance+is+increasingly+measured&index=1&md5=6dbabad39ef9ea92ffb1ebaaf79f2472) by the number of concurrent agents a rack can sustain at target latency – and Xeon helps maximize that delivered work by keeping data flowing, tools executing and accelerators fed. **Intel GPU D-Series: Purpose-Built for Efficient Inference at Scale** [Intel GPU D-series](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%...

LLMs.content: # Microsoft releases 'Microsoft-Decision-1,' a decision model similar to Jev's. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/00_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/10/13/microsoft-decision-1/00.png) Microsoft released its decision-making model, ' **Microsoft-Decision-1,** ' on October 9, 2026, local time. It has been reported that in a task analyzing game reviews, it achieved quality equivalent to GPT-6 Sol while being more than 14 times faster and costing less than 1/200th of GPT-6 Sol. **Microsoft-Decision-1: Our model for fast decision-making** <https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry/> > Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our new model for fast decision-making. > > It delivers top performance on structured decision tasks, outperforming both LLMs and other decision models in latency and quality. > > We're already testing it across Microsoft for everything from incident… [pic.twitter.com/M3fAOD90r6](https://t.co/M3fAOD90r6) > > — Satya Nadella (@satyanadella) [October 9, 2026](https://x.com/satyanadella/status/2108627923888754862?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) Decision-making models are AI models with a significantly different design from large-scale language models (LLMs). By pre-defining multiple options, they can perform the operation of 'selecting the appropriate answer to a question from the options and outputting it along with a confidence score' quickly and at low cost. Decision-making models have attracted considerable attention since the release of 'Jev' in September 2026, and numerous similar models have since emerged. **[ChatGPT co-developer develops AI model 'Jev' that processes data using a different method than LLM, enabling low-cost and ultra-fast task execution with GPT-5.6 Terra-level performance - GIGAZINE](https://gigazine.net/news/20260916-system-one-jev/)** ![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/09/16/system-one-jev/00.png) Microsoft announced a Jev-like decision-making model called 'Microsoft-Decision-1' on October 9, 2026. Microsoft-Decision-1 is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, validation, and workflow control, and can be easily integrated into existing application agent workflows in a secure and reliable environment. According to Microsoft, Microsoft-Decision-1 achieved the highest accuracy in 36 benchmark comparisons, including approximately 150,000 tests that included benchmark questions not used during training. It also recorded the fastest time in the benchmark tests, being 2.5 times faster than the next fastest, H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1, and 35 times faster than GPT-6 Sol. LLMs.content: ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_alone_header.svg) ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_simplified_unicolor_t.svg) ![dark mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/moon-filled.svg) ![light mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/sun-filled.svg) ![EN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![DE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/de.svg) ![US Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![ES Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/es.svg) ![FR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/fr.svg) ![IT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/it.svg) ![NL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/nl.svg) ![PL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pl.svg) ![PT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pt.svg) ![RU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/ru.svg) ![TR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/tr.svg) ![SE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/se.svg) ![CN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/cn.svg) ![HU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/hu.svg) # Intel's new GPU packs up to 480GB of memory — but skips 3D graphics ![Intel GPU D270 — an AI accelerator designed for inference workloads.](fileadmin/_processed_/e/3/csm_intel_gpu_D270_ai_01_e8e2e50240.jpg) Intel has revealed the first accelerator in its GPU D-series, previously known by the codename Crescent Island: the D270, a data-center card built for AI inference rather than conventional 3D graphics. Based on Intel’s Xe3P architecture, the accelerator can be configured with up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory. One of the accelerator’s most unusual features is its memory configuration. Intel’s own reference card comes with 160GB of LPDDR5X, while its manufacturing partners can develop versions with up to 480GB. Rather than using high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as many competing AI accelerators do, the D270 relies on LPDDR5X. Intel is prioritizing memory capacity and deployment costs for inference workloads, where large language models need substantial amounts of memory to store model weights and manage long conversations. The accelerator offers 1.5TB/s of memory bandwidth and a peak FP8 performance of 1.3 petaflops. It has a 350W power target and uses an air-cooled PCIe 5.0 x16 design, allowing it to fit into conventional server infrastructure without requiring specialized liquid-cooling systems. The GPU contains 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines for accelerated matrix operations and 32MB of unified L2 cache. Intel has removed conventional 3D-graphics and ray-tracing hardware, allowing more silicon area to be dedicated to compute and AI processing. Consequently, the D270 is not a gaming graphics card, despite being based on GPU technology. Intel says the GPU D-series is intended for large language models, long-context inference and services that handle multiple AI requests concurrently. A single card can accommodate models with up to roughly 300 billion parameters, while a server equipped with eight accelerators can support models exceeding one trillion parameters. Intel lists potential uses including agentic AI, enterprise assistants, coding assistants, document understanding, multimodal AI, diffusion models and high-concurrency serving. Intel says customer sampling is underway with server manufacturers, cloud providers and software vendors. The company has not announced pricing or a general availability date for the GPU D-series. ![The Intel GPU D270 is based on a relatively compact GPU that lacks dedicated 3D-graphics and ray-tracing hardware](fileadmin/_processed_/7/3/csm_intel_gpu_D270_ai_02_cda3ed4082.jpg) ## Source(s) [Intel](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/newsroom/news/artificial-intelligence/intel-accelerates-open-infrastructure-agentic-ai-era.html) ![Google Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/google_logo.svg) ![Facebook Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/facebook_logo.svg) ![Threads Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/threa...

Attorneys can now use AI-powered platforms to summarize deposition transcripts, organize discovery, draft contracts and generate preliminary research in a fraction of the time previously required. Technology vendors promise enormous gains in efficiency and client service. Against this backdrop, AI’s capabilities resurrect a familiar question with newly urgent stakes: When lawyers or clients share information with an AI platform, how do we ensure traditional protections such as the [attorney-client privilege](https://valawyersweekly.com/tag/attorney-client-privilege/?taxo-tag-body "Posts tagged with Attorney-client privilege") or the [work product doctrine](https://valawyersweekly.com/tag/work-product-doctrine/?taxo-tag-body "Posts tagged with work product doctrine") continue to apply? For centuries, privilege has rested on a simple premise: Clients must be able to communicate candidly with their lawyers without fear that those communications will later be disclosed. The doctrine has survived revolutions in communication — from handwritten correspondence to email — because its focus has never been the technology through which communications occur. Rather, privilege depends upon a confidential attorney-client relationship and communications made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice. Generative AI presents the next major test of that principle. Two 2026 court rulings offer signposts for how these questions will be analyzed, and how firms and companies should leverage AI tools while protecting privilege. **Privilege protects relationships, not conversations about the law** The privilege protects confidential communications between attorney and client, ensuring the uninhibited candor required to give and receive sound legal advice. The work product doctrine likewise shields materials prepared by or for counsel in anticipation of litigation, so that counsel can work without fear of disclosing legal theories and strategy. Both doctrines depend on more than the mere discussion of legal issues; they build on particular legal relationships, defined purposes, and an expectation of [confidentiality](https://valawyersweekly.com/tag/confidentiality/?taxo-tag-body "Posts tagged with confidentiality"). Open Source AI.content: There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [Subscribe](https://petapixel.com/members) [Sign In](https://petapixel.com/login/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fpetapixel.com%2F2026%2F10%2F12%2Fthere-are-free-open-source-versions-of-microsoft-office-apps-thanks-to-ai%2F) # There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [News](https://petapixel.com/topic/news/) [Jeremy Gray](https://petapixel.com/author/jeremygray/) * Copied! Brandon Thomas, the experienced software engineer behind the AI-assisted reverse engineering effort to [rebuild open-source versions of Adobe’s Creative Suite applications](https://petapixel.com/2026/10/07/someone-rebuilt-free-open-source-versions-of-photoshop-premiere-and-lightroom-using-ai/), including Photoshop, Premiere, and Lightroom, is setting his sights on another oft-maligned set of software: Microsoft Office. As Thomas’ ArtCraft Discord has grown considerably with the release and publicity surrounding his Adobe clones, the developer has been taking requests for which software to reverse engineer next using Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 AI LLM. Unsurprisingly, many people, like they are sick of paying for Adobe’s software, are tired of paying for Microsoft Office, including Microsoft Word and Excel. ![A Microsoft Word document titled ](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/review_1-800x500.jpg) Microsoft Word gets rebuilt using AI. It’s now “WordCraft,” and open source. Thomas took the request and quickly started work on open-source Microsoft Office clones for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Word clone, WordCraft, looks practically identical. The same goes for the Excel clone, GridCraft, and the PowerPoint look-alike, DeckCraft. Thomas is also working on an AutoCAD clone and a studio-grade audio mixer, SoundCraft. In response to criticism that he is churning out AI slop, [Thomas took to X](https://x.com/echelon) to tout his credentials. “My guy, I can code,” Thomas said in response to online criticism. “AI models enable me to work as an entire company. I’m doing 4x better than Google’s revenue per employee.” ![A spreadsheet titled Quarterly Sales Dashboard showing regional sales data, a bar chart comparing revenue by region, and a pie chart showing the share of annual total.](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/hero-2_1-800x500.jpg) ArtCraft’s Excel clone, GridCraft “AI enables people to do far more. To have bolder ambition, to accomplish incredible tasks without tiring,” Thomas continues. “If you put down the hate and try the tools, you’ll find the energy to become the best version of yourself.” In this case, the ambition is to reverse engineer functionally identical versions of premium, paid software built by people over decades and release them as free, open-source applications. That said, not everything here is free. There are [subscriptions](https://getartcraft.com/pricing) for using generative AI features inside the ArtCraft software suite. For example, creating about 220 4K-quality Nano Banana Pro images requires a Max subscription, which is currently about $48 per month thanks to a 20% launch discount. This subscription nets users 413 seconds, or less than seven minutes, of generative video inside Seedance 2.0. ![A PowerPoint slide titled ](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/dark-mode_1-800x500.jpg) The PowerPoint clone, DeckCraft It’s hard to predict what’s next, but if paid software exists that enough people don’t want to pay for, it seems like a good candidate for Thomas’ AI-powered reverse engineering mission. “Tell us what to rebuild next,” ArtCraft says. --- Image creditsArtCraft. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English #AI # QGIS Bans AI-Generated Contributions After Maintainer Burnout • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •2 min read Share this article The QGIS project has adopted a strict policy prohibiting AI-generated code and content contributions, reversing its previous 'human in the loop' approach after maintainers reported unsustainable review burdens and erosion of community trust. The QGIS project has formally banned all AI-generated contributions, marking a sharp reversal from its earlier policy that permitted AI-assisted work with human oversight. The change, enacted through QGIS Enhancement Proposal 428 (QEP428), passed a community vote this week and takes effect immediately. Core developer Nyall Dawson proposed the ban after maintainers faced what they described as an unmanageable flood of AI-generated pull requests. The previous policy, QEP408, required contributors to tag AI-assisted work and maintain a "human in the loop." In practice, the tagging system failed — roughly 50 PRs carried the AI-assisted label, and about 40 were closed without merging. Others slipped through untagged. "AI use from external contributors puts a massive and unbearable pressure on the shoulders of our maintainers, who already had a tough job before the era of LLMs," wrote QGIS PSC member Julien Cabieces (haubourg) in the discussion. "AI stream is a lot higher than what human review can take seriously, leading to either a longer list of un-reviewed PRs or not fully reviewed code and quality issues." The project lost at least one high-value contributor due to the strain, according to Dawson. The new policy adopts a "closed door" approach: all AI-generated contributions are prohibited, with the possibility of narrowly reopening specific use cases — such as IDE autocomplete or language translation — only after careful case-by-case discussion. Contributor Amalvir, who had submitted AI-assisted bug fixes, supported the ban: "By doing this, we've broken a trust contract between the reviewer and the contributor. The contract that, to contribute at such a big project, you know what you're doing." Not all feedback was unanimous. Developer Kannes argued the policy's broad wording — "assisted" and "used" — could inadvertently block legitimate uses like AI-assisted code review, security auditing, or learning unfamiliar codebases. Dawson acknowledged the risk: "Yes, we are aware we might throw the baby with the bathwater, but the baby might be non-viable." The policy's enforcement relies on contributor honesty. As PSC chair Tim Sutton (timlinux) put it: "The measure of compliance is 'did you in good conscience write the code yourself' — we are not set up to peer into your computer." The ban extends beyond code to documentation, bug reports, discussions, PR descriptions, and all written interactions on GitHub. The QEP repository itself is also covered. QGIS joins a growing list of open-source projects restricting AI contributions, including the Linux kernel, which in 2024 warned maintainers about AI-generated patches that wasted reviewer time. The difference: QGIS has made the prohibition explicit policy rather than informal guidance. The project plans to revisit specific exemptions at its upcoming user conference. For now, the door is shut. He was responding to recent debates about slowing AI development, which have been hotly discussed among U.S. AI companies. Known as one of the “three godfathers of AI,” he is one of the researchers who laid the foundation for today’s AI capabilities in recognizing cats or text in images. He visited Korea to attend the “Industrial AI Global Cooperation Meeting,” hosted by Aitomatic and the International Industrial AI Conference (IIAC) 2026 Organizing Committee, and organized by AI Alliance and ASI Foundry. Open Source AI.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### October 12, 2026 ### October 9, 2026 ### October 8, 2026 ### October 7, 2026 ## H2O-Lightning-4B Ranks 1st on JevBench Open-Weights Leaderboard *A 4-billion-parameter open-source decision model finishes ahead of 103 open-weight systems, including some built on base models nearly eight times its size, on a benchmark that weighs intelligence, calibration, speed and cost equally.* MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 — [H2O.ai](https://h2o.ai/), the trusted Sovereign AI Platform for predictive, generative and agentic AI, with observability built in, today announced that **H2O-Lightning-4B**, its open-weights decision model, ranked first among 104 open-weight systems on the [JevBench Composite Score leaderboard](https://h2o.ai/blog/2026/h2o-lightning-jevbench/) as of Oct. 7. The model scores 72.5 out of 100, above the 71.5 posted by Jev, the benchmark’s closed API reference system, at an estimated $0.021 per 1,000 decisions. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px.jpg)Much of the AI work inside banks, insurers, health systems, telcos and government agencies is a decision about a record: route this ticket, flag this clause, score this claim. TypeSafe AI built Jev around that idea. Jev is a model that answers a typed question with a calibrated probability instead of generated text. Each decision needs the right answer, a probability a risk team can set a threshold on, a latency that fits a live workflow, and a cost that stays predictable at millions of calls a month. JevBench scores all four on an equal-weight harmonic mean, so a weak axis drags down the whole score. An open 4-billion-parameter model scoring above a closed reference system is the shift regulated buyers have been waiting for. Owning the model no longer means giving up quality. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg) “Better decisions don’t need bigger models. Classification is one of the most common enterprise use cases, and models like H2O-Lightning deliver frontier-model quality and lightning-fast decisions at about 100 times lower cost. Leading AI companies, including Microsoft, are now building decision models of their own. This is not a flash in the pan,” said Sri Ambati, Founder and CEO of H2O.ai. **How It Works** H2O-Lightning-4B is a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B. It answers typed decision questions about a record such as a document, ticket, policy or conversation, and returns a probability for every option. It supports three question types: choice (one of a set of named options), yes/no (the probability that a statement is true) and score (an ordinal level on a stated scale, with its probability distribution). Each decision is one forward pass and one output token, so cost is driven by input tokens alone. The model runs on unmodified vLLM 0.30.0 with a small standard-library shim in front. **The Results** H2O-Lightning-4B competes in a crowded, fast-moving field. TypeSafe AI set the bar with Jev. The model scores 72.5 out of 100, above the 71.5 posted by Jev, the benchmark’s closed API reference system, at an estimated $0.021 per 1,000 decisions. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px.jpg)Much of the AI work inside banks, insurers, health systems, telcos and government agencies is a decision about a record: route this ticket, flag this clause, score this claim. TypeSafe AI built Jev around that idea. Jev is a model that answers a typed question with a calibrated probability instead of generated text. Each decision needs the right answer, a probability a risk team can set a threshold on, a latency that fits a live workflow, and a cost that stays predictable at millions of calls a month. JevBench scores all four on an equal-weight harmonic mean, so a weak axis drags down the whole score. An open 4-billion-parameter model scoring above a closed reference system is the shift regulated buyers have been waiting for. Owning the model no longer means giving up quality. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg) “Better decisions don’t need bigger models. Classification is one of the most common enterprise use cases, and models like H2O-Lightning deliver frontier-model quality and lightning-fast decisions at about 100 times lower cost. Leading AI companies, including Microsoft, are now building decision models of their own. This is not a flash in the pan,” said Sri Ambati, Founder and CEO of H2O.ai. **How It Works** H2O-Lightning-4B is a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B. It answers typed decision questions about a record such as a document, ticket, policy or conversation, and returns a probability for every option. It supports three question types: choice (one of a set of named options), yes/no (the probability that a statement is true) and score (an ordinal level on a stated scale, with its probability distribution). Each decision is one forward pass and one output token, so cost is driven by input tokens alone. I recently started my tenth company as technical founder. I'm also co-founder and chairman of Saigon A.I., a doctoral researcher at the University of St Andrews working between educational psychology and artificial intelligence with a focus on self-regulated learning (SRL), and the builder of QCoda, an AI governance platform focused on governing AI-assisted software engineering. QCoda started with a pattern I kept running into, in my own teams and in teams I advised. We'd make a dozen consequential decisions while planning an AI feature. Which model. Which data. Where it runs. Who gets to see the prompts. Nobody wrote any of it down. Months later an auditor (or a customer's security team, or a regulator) would ask why we did it that way, and the honest answer was that nobody really decided. It just happened. Governance showed up after the mistake, as punishment. That's the lens I bring here. Almost every AI architecture conversation I have now includes one of three words: *sovereign*, *decentralized* or *private perimeter*. People use them interchangeably. They shouldn't. Each one answers a different question and protects a different party, and none of them answers the question that actually gets teams in trouble. Open Source AI.titleZh: OCP Summit 2026: Powering AI with Open Innovations in Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across Networks - Engineering at Meta
Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#content) POSTED ON TO [Data Center Engineering](https://engineering.fb.com/category/data-center-engineering/), [Data Infrastructure](https://engineering.fb.com/category/data-infrastructure/), [DevInfra](https://engineering.fb.com/category/developer-tools/), [ML Applications](https://engineering.fb.com/category/ml-applications/), [Networking & Traffic](https://engineering.fb.com/category/networking-traffic/), [Open Source](https://engineering.fb.com/category/open-source/) # OCP Summit 2026: Powering AI with Open Innovations in Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across Networks ![](https://engineering.fb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Meta-OCP-2026.jpg "Meta OCP 2026") * At the 2026 Open Compute Project Global Summit, Meta is sharing the next generation of open networking infrastructure, including:  + Our first liquid-cooled network rack (IcePack), and 102.4T switch platform (IceCube). + Flattened Planar Fabric (FPF), a multiplane backend scale-out fabric that fundamentally changes how GPUs connect to the network + MetaRoCE, our open-source AI transport protocol. + Launching the Open Switch Platform Architecture (OSPA) initiative within OCP. * We’re inviting engineers, silicon vendors, system integrators, and operators to join us and the OCP community in meeting the challenges of building open, efficient, and sustainable AI infrastructure. At Meta, we believe that open networking is critical for building high-performance, scalable, and sustainable infrastructure, and we’ve acted on that conviction since co-founding the Open Compute Project (OCP) in 2011.  Throughout the ongoing AI revolution, Meta has pushed the boundaries of what’s possible in data center networking and shared our advances with the industry. At OCP 2025, [we introduced](https://engineering.fb.com/2025/10/13/data-infrastructure/ocp-summit-2025-the-open-future-of-networking-hardware-for-ai/) our latest AI scale-out fabrics and drove the creation of the [Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking (ESUN)](https://www.opencompute.org/news/introducing-esun-advancing-ethernet-for-scale-up-ai-infrastructure-at-ocp/) initiative. This year at OCP 2026, we’re sharing the networking innovations that directly support our latest AI workloads such as Meta’s [Muse Wonder](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/10/introducing-muse-wonder-models/) and [Muse Spark](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2) models, and [Muse, our personal AI agent built for everyone](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). Here’s some of what’s new: * **The 102.4T scale-out switch**: Meta’s first liquid-cooled network rack (IcePack) and 102.4T switch blades (IceCube), designed to support high power density, deliver higher thermal efficiency, and enable gigawatt-scale AI clusters. * **The scale-out Flattened Planar Fabric (FPF)**: Meta’s multiplane fabric, enabling larger, highly efficient GPU clusters with lower latency — with learnings shared with our cloud partners. * **Scale-across for multi-site clusters**: Meta’s [petabit-scale backend aggregation (BAG) super-spine](https://engineering.fb.com/2026/02/09/data-center-engineering/building-prometheus-how-backend-aggregation-enables-gigawatt-scale-ai-clusters/) and how large-scale training jobs deal with failures at this scale — with an overview of how we’ve built SRv6 regional backbones using FBOSS and SAI to handle even longer distances * **Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking:** Meta’s MTIA 300 system uses Tahan, an Ethernet-based 51.2T scale-up switch, delivering 6.4 Tbps per accelerator — with a preview of next-gen 72-accelerator-per-rack design on 102.4T silicon and moving toward an ESUN-based implementation with future chips. * **Open Switch Platform Architecture (OSPA)**: a new OCP initiative, co-led by Meta, Microsoft, and Alibaba, that standardizes the switch platform layer — with specification v1.0 now submitted to OCP. * [**MetaRoCE**](https://engineering.fb.com/2026/08/24/networki...

Infra & Chips.content: Updated : Tuesday, October 13, 2026, 10:29 * [Home](/) * [Login](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/member/login.html) * [Sign in](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/member/index.html) * [Korean](/?editcode=MAIN_13) [![Businesskorea](/image/logo/toplogo_20230426040837.png) ![](/image/logo/year_40.png)](/) [![Businesskorea](/image/logo/printlogo_20230426040837.png)](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr) MangoBoost Teams Up With AMD to Challenge Nvidia in AI Inference Scroll Move Status-bar # MangoBoost Teams Up With AMD to Challenge Nvidia in AI Inference * *Editor* Park Jung-hwan * 2026.10.13 09:48 ## Korean Startup Unveils Serverless AI Platform, Targets 500MW Infrastructure Expansion ![AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su speaks at an AI semiconductor industry roundtable held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Jongno-gu, Seoul, on Oct. 7, 2026.](/news/photo/202610/278642_286325_475.jpg) AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su speaks at an AI semiconductor industry roundtable held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Jongno-gu, Seoul, on Oct. 7, 2026. South Korean AI infrastructure startup MangoBoost is expanding its collaboration with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) as it seeks to challenge Nvidia’s dominance in the artificial intelligence market through an integrated approach to hardware, software and AI inference services. AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su has highlighted the startup as an example of AI infrastructure development in South Korea, underscoring the growing relationship between the two companies. Kim Jang-woo, CEO of MangoBoost and a professor at Seoul National University, unveiled the company's new AI inference platform, Mango Inference, during a press conference at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 12. “MangoBoost is no longer simply a component company,” Kim said, announcing the company's transformation into an AI factory operator that designs and integrates hardware and software to deliver AI services directly to customers. Mango Inference is a serverless inference service that enables businesses and developers to access AI models using a single API key without building their own server infrastructure. Users can select open-weight models, including DeepSeek and GLM, and pay according to usage. The company said its proprietary inference optimization software, LLMBooost, reduces bottlenecks in data transfers between storage devices and GPUs, lowering costs by at least 20% compared with existing high-performance services. A central element of MangoBoost's expansion strategy is its close collaboration with AMD, which is competing with Nvidia in the AI GPU market. While AMD has been working to strengthen its networking and software ecosystem, MangoBoost contributes system-level design and optimization capabilities. The companies' joint technical achievements have also been featured on AMD's official blog. During her visit to South Korea on Oct. 7, Su cited MangoBoost as a notable example of domestic AI infrastructure development and maintained close communication with Kim, according to the company. Kim said the relationship has also strengthened MangoBoost's ability to secure GPU supplies. He explained that the company has established a roadmap for obtaining a stable supply of AMD's latest GPUs and has drawn up plans to procure tens of thousands of units. To improve service reliability and operational efficiency, MangoBoost is building a 1-megawatt (MW) AI infrastructure facility near Dosan Park in Seoul's Gangnam district. The facility is already partially operational, with AMD's latest Instinct-series GPUs being introduced in phases. Full completion is targeted for the first quarter of 2027. By increasing the proportion of internally designed systems, MangoBoost aims to reduce its reliance on external cloud providers and improve overall operating efficiency. SambaNova’s Forge Price reached $70.13 per share on Oct. 12, up 259.27% over one year, according to [Forge Global](https://forgeglobal.com/sambanova-systems_stock/). That puts its indicative share price at roughly 3.6 times its level a year earlier. By comparison, NVIDIA delivered a 23.73% one-year total return as of Oct. 12, including dividends and other distributions, according to [data](https://www.perplexity.ai/finance/NVDA) from Perplexity Finance. SambaNova’s percentage gain was more than 10 times NVIDIA’s return over the period. The comparison comes as investors pour money into the computing infrastructure needed to train and run increasingly capable AI models. ## Competing for AI Compute SambaNova and NVIDIA compete in AI computing, particularly in the market for hardware used to run AI models, known as inference. However, the companies have different approaches to the market. Microsoft’s Maia 300 isn’t a Nvidia killer – it’s a power play By [Diana Goovaerts](/person/diana-goovaerts-2) Oct 12, 2026 1:02pm [Microsoft](/keywords/microsoft) [GPU](/keyword/gpu) [inference](/keyword/inference) [artificial intelligence (AI)](/keyword/artificial-intelligence-ai) ![Maia 300 chip](https://qtxasset.com/cdn-cgi/image/w=850,h=478,f=auto,fit=crop,g=0.5x0.5/https://qtxasset.com/quartz/qcloud4/media/image/maia_300_microsoft.png?VersionId=1Dl_ot06FaFH5VIjmI3V4o1EZtmjjOJT) Microsoft's new Maia 300 chip is all about delivering inference efficiently - and for good reason. (Microsoft) * **Microsoft’s new Maia 300 chip is built for AI inference at scale** * **Maia 300 ties compute, memory and networking into one AI-optimized system** * **By optimizing for tokens per megawatt, Microsoft is solving for its data center power problem** [Microsoft](https://www.fierce-network.com/keywords/microsoft) wants to run more of its own services on its in-house inferencing chips, announcing plans to scale deployments of its Maia system into multi-gigawatt territory in 2027 to handle workloads from Copilot, GitHub and Foundry. But that doesn’t necessarily mean it is looking to cut into Nvidia and AMD’s market share, as much as some would like to frame it that way. “I don't expect Maia to slow Nvidia or AMD deployments across Azure,” Moor Insights and Strategy VP and Principal Analyst Matt Kimball [wrote](http://linkedin.com/pulse/microsoft-azure-maia-300-ai-chip-your-business-never-pick-kimball-jvxqc/). “Even with massive Trainium deployments, AWS signed a $38 billion agreement with OpenAI built on Nvidia systems. AI demand is growing too fast for any single supply chain.” So why, then, is Microsoft doing this? It all comes down to efficiency. Microsoft announced its plans [alongside the launch](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/10/12/microsoft-to-expand-azure-maia-system-to-multi-gigawatt-deployments/) of its Maia 300 chip, the third generation of its custom in-house silicon. Notably, Maia boasts a software-defined dataflow architecture and AI-assisted kernel optimization to minimize data movement and improve utilization of compute, memory and networking resources. Maia 300’s 18 TBps of peak memory bandwidth is also more than double Maia 200’s 7 TBps, helping it perform better on long-context workloads and large models. Infra & Chips.content: # Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs The new Maia 300 chip will start rolling out to production AI workloads in 2027. The new Maia 300 chip will start rolling out to production AI workloads in 2027. Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the “primary AI inference system” for Microsoft’s products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it’s also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks. Maia 300 will start being rolled out to production in 2027, and it has been designed with efficiency in mind. “We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems,” says Scott Guthrie, executive vice president of Microsoft’s cloud group. “And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200.” These efficiency improvements will allow Microsoft to rely mainly on its in-house AI chips soon, instead of ones from Nvidia and AMD. “We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary AI inference system for Microsoft products and services,” says Guthrie. Maia 300 is a successor to the 200, which was only announced in January. Maia 200 is already running on production AI workloads across Microsoft, including Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft’s own AI models. “Maia 200 is the best performing AI infrastructure in our fleet, measured in real world metrics for AI services,” says Guthrie. “Maia 300 is a complete AI system designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today: Long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences, and sustained, multi-step agentic tasks.” Microsoft is using a new chiplet architecture to get its all-important efficiency gains. Built on TSMC’s N2P process node, the latest Maia 300 architecture separates compute, memory controller, and I/O functions. “This increases the silicon area dedicated to compute performance and allows each function to use the technology best suited to its role,” says the Azure hardware and infrastructure team. Maia 300 is also a key part of Microsoft’s own AI model work, and could help the company achieve its goal of catching up with Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic. “We have to work across the full stack, all the way down to the silicon,” says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. “At that scale we need a platform that we own, and that we co-design with our models. That’s why running our Microsoft AI models on top of the Maia chip is a critical focus for our team.” * Tom Warren
